chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from Abī Jaʿfar, from Abī Ṭālib ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Dāwūd ibn Abī Yazīd — and he is Dāwūd ibn Farqad — from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When the sun has set, then the time of maghrib has entered, until there passes the amount of time in which one praying would perform three rakʿahs. Then when that has passed, the time of maghrib and the later ʿisha has entered, until there remains before midnight the amount of time in which one praying would perform four rakʿahs. Then when that amount remains, the time of maghrib has gone out, and the time of the later ʿisha remains until midnight.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ: the measure of time equal to performing four rakʿahs
key_terms.الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ: the later night prayer, meaning ʿisha
key_terms.انْتِصَافِ اللَّيْلِ: midnight; the terminal point mentioned for the prayer time
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ رَكَعَاتٍ: the measure of time equal to performing three rakʿahs
key_terms.غَابَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun set; the beginning marker for maghrib time
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْمَغْرِبِ: the prescribed time of the maghrib prayer

ai.seo_question: When does the time of maghrib end and the time of ʿisha last until according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal timing of maghrib and ʿisha prayers. It states that maghrib begins at sunset, then after the duration of three rakʿahs both maghrib and ʿisha share time, and when only the duration of four rakʿahs remains before midnight, maghrib time ends and ʿisha continues until midnight.
